correctness.rationale: For a strict lower record at integer value \(\ell\), the next record value is distributed as the parent law conditioned on \(X<\ell\), whose normalizing probability is \(F(\ell-1)\). Multiplying these exact transitions gives the corrected likelihood. The source uses \(F(\ell)\), which includes ties and produces a parameter-dependent likelihood ratio. The packaged DAPW checker verifies transition normalization and the three-record numerical example.

value.rationale: The mixed upper-lower record design is presented as one of the paper's three main inferential contributions and is compared against Type-II censoring and upper records in simulation, Bayesian estimation, and bootstrap intervals. Because the missing lattice shift is parameter-dependent, it changes the inferential target rather than merely rescaling the likelihood. The correction is therefore central to the validity of the mixed-record comparisons and stress-strength estimates.
